newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says Gulf oil terminal at full capacity.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says Gulf oil terminal at full capacity.

text.p: Iraq's Mina al-Bakr oil terminal in the Gulf can now work at full capacity estimated at 1.6 million barrels per day (bpd), the official Iraqi News Agency INA said on Tuesday.
"The capacity of Mina al-Bakr, one of Iraq's main ports, is 1.6 million bpd and can receive oil tankers with loading capacity ranging from 60,000 to 350,000 tonnes," INA said.

The terminal, heavily damaged during the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait, is handling up to 250,000 bpd of the 550,000 bpd Iraq is allowed by the U.N. to export under an oil-for-food deal signed with the world body.
Iraq is permitted to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months to buy humanitarian needs for the Iraqi people.
Two weeks ago it started pumping about 350,000 bpd for export through the Turkish terminal of Ceyhan, unleashing the first Iraqi oil exports since the Gulf crisis erupted in 1990.
Baghdad is allowed to export only from Ceyhan and Mina al-Bakr under U.N.-approved contracts.
